'''Vladilen Fyodorovich Minin''' ({{langx|ru|Влади́лен Фёдорович Ми́нин}}; born 27 May 1932, Rudinka, [[Ryazan Oblast]]) is a Soviet and Russian [[physicist]], [[Doctor of Sciences|Doctor of Technical Sciences]], a [[professor]], a member of the Academy of Technological Sciences of the Russian Federation. He was the founder, general director and chief designer of the Institute of [[Applied physics|Applied Physics]] (1966-1996), the founder and president of the Urals-Siberian Branch of Russian Academy of Technological Sciences. He developed air- and navy- launched missiles, custom control and safety systems and computer equipment.

== Biography ==
He was born to a family of [[teacher]]s in the village of Rudinka, [[Ryazan Oblast]]. Later the Minin family moved to Nagishy (Lebyazhy Usad) of Gorlovka village settlement in Skopin district of [[Ryazan Oblast]]. After his father's return from the [[World War II|Second World War]], the Minin family moved to [[Moscow]]. Vladilen finished secondary school for working youth No. 77 in Stalin district of Moscow, then he studied in industrial school No. 40 to become a metal turner. He worked as a turner at the plant, then as a lab assistant in science classrooms of the school for working youth and taught physics to militiamen.<ref name="Minin">{{cite journal |date=2002 |title= Vladilen Fyodorovich Minin |url=https://cyberleninka.ru/article/n/vladilen-fedorovich-minin |language= ru |journal= Computer Optics |issue= 22 |pages= 5–6 }}</ref>

=== Alma mater ===
V.Minin graduated from [[Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology]]. His graduate work was devoted to the research of a high-voltage electric discharge in liquid. V.S. Komelkov (one of the chief of the Department of Atomic Energy Institute) who refereed his theses and later offered him the work in his department.

=== Siberian Branch of the Russian Academy of Sciences ===
In 1958, at the invitation of [[Mikhail Lavrentyev]], Minin moved to Novosibirsk Akademgorodok (scientific centre) to work at [[Lavrentyev Institute of Hydrodynamics]] of the Siberian Branch of the Russian Academy of Sciences. He initiated some new research directions : electromagnetic throwing of the body, shock waves interaction with bubbles in water with air layers, anomalous properties of nitrogen plasma, explosive sound sources, explosion plume, etc.<ref name="The Institute of Hydrodynamics ">{{cite book |last= Vasilyev  |first= А.А.|date= 2017|title= Institute of Hydrodynamics: people, deeds, dates…|language= ru|location= Novosibirsk |publisher= Academic publishing house «Geo»}}</ref><ref name="Minin 2">[http://www.soran1957.ru/?id=PA_Users_pavl_634395045572656250_2707 Minin Vladilen Fyodorovich ]</ref> At that time the research in these fields was not being conducted in any other laboratory of the Institute of Hydrodynamics.

He discovered the effect of the cumulative jet formation when a gas bubble collapses under the action of a shock wave and proposed a method for dissolving gases in a liquid based on this effect.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Minin | first1=I.V. | last2=Minin | first2=O.V. | title=The breakup of gas bubbles by a shock wave: brief historical background| journal= Eur. Phys. J. H| volume=49 | date=2024 | issue=5 | doi=10.1140/epjh/s13129-024-00071-w| pages=4–10| bibcode=2024EPJH...49....5M }}</ref>

In 2005 professor Christopher Earls Brennen published his monograph «Cavitation and Bubble Dynamics» where special focus was given to the research of shock waves interaction with gas bubbles in water and experimental discovery of cumulative jet formation effect in case of bubble collapse conducted by Minin.

Minin initiated a new direction for the research, i.e. experimental study of solitary wave propagation features in the shallows as applied to tsunami.<ref name=" Explosion on liquid surface ">{{cite journal |last= Minin |first= Vladilen |date=1964 |title= Explosion on liquid surface |language= ru|journal= Applied Mechanics and Applied Physics }}</ref>

In 1959 (by the order of Lavrentyev) Minin was appointed the chief engineer to be responsible for the construction and provision of scientific instruments made in his laboratory not only for the Institute of Hydrodynamics, but also for other institutes to-be-built for the Siberian Branch of [[Russian Academy of Sciences]].

In 1961 Minin passed his defense for a degree of a candidate of technical sciences.<ref name=" Underwater shock wave interaction with bubble curtain: theses ">{{cite book |last= Minin |first= Vladilen |date= 1961|title= Underwater shock wave interaction with bubble curtain: theses |language= ru|location= Novosibirsk |publisher= Institute of Hydrodinamics, Russian Academy of Sciences }}</ref> In his theses he offered to apply explosion for low-soluble gas dilution in water.<ref name="Blast creator">{{cite journal |last= Kuznetsov|first=V. |date= 1961|title=Blast creator |url=http://www.sbras.info/system/files/archive/archive1961-2009/1961_22.pdf |language= ru|journal= Za Nauku V Sibiri (For Science in Siberia) }}</ref>

In 1963 Minin was conferred a degree of a senior research assistant in chemical physics of the [[Academy of Sciences of the Soviet Union]].<ref>Decision of  the Presidium of the USSR Academy of Sciences, 24 May 1963</ref>

In 1963-1964 he started working on branch-oriented optoelectronic systems.

[[File:Keldish-teplo.jpg|thumb|Vladilen Minin and [[Mstislav Keldysh]] (President of the Academy of Sciences of the Soviet Union) testing “Teplo”]]
 
At the same period he delivered lectures to his first students at the preliminary courses of [[Novosibirsk State University]]. Later he was invited by Vice-rector [[Rem Soloukhin]] to take part in establishing demonstration hall for the Department of General Physics and practical physics. Over 100 demonstration scenarios for a course in physics were made by Minin. In 1959-1969 he worked as an associate professor at the Department of General Physics.<ref name=" Nauka. Academgorodok. University.   Reminiscences. Essays. Interview ">{{cite journal |editor1-first=N.S. |editor1-last=Dikansky |editor2-first=N.V. |editor2-last=Dulepova |editor3-first=V.V. |editor3-last=Radchenko |date=1999 |title= Take personal responsibility |language= ru|journal= Nauka. Academgorodok. University. Reminiscences. Essays. Interview }}</ref>

=== Institute of Applied Physics ===
In 1966 Minin established a State Special Design Bureau (later renamed into “Sosna”) for radio-electronic solutions. In 1968 the bureau was reorganized into the Institute of Applied Physics and he became the head of it. He was to mobilize various institutes of the Siberian Branch of [[Russian Academy of Sciences]] around common work on diversification and branch-oriented fundamental research and pilot works.

In 1973 the Institute proceeded with the execution of additional objectives set by the head organization of the Ministry of Machine-Building i.e. development of aircraft-launch rockets. At the same time (the period of preparation for [[1980 Summer Olympics|Moscow 1980 Summer Olympic Games]]) by the government order the Institute was to develop and produce the series of [[X-ray]] security systems, explosive detectors (a range of gas analyzers М01, М02) and explosion-proof facilities and other systems.<ref name="History of technical protection">{{cite book |last= S. E. Shipilov and V. P. Yakubov |date=2018 |title= History of technical protection. 60 years in science: to the jubilee of Prof. V.F. Minin |publisher= IOP Conf. Series: Materials Science and Engineering}}</ref>

In the late 1970s – the early 1980s joint works with the laboratory of millimeter and submillimeter-wave metrics (Institute of Radio Engineering and Electronics of [[Academy of Sciences of the Soviet Union]]) were started. These were the research works on millimeter and submillimeter wave range for transmission and [[reflection spectrum#materials science|reflection]] spectra of the explosives and their simulators. For the first time measurements of their spectral characteristics were determined. Collaborative works directed by V.F. Minin were started to develop high-quality non-aberrational quasi-optical lens of submillimeter-wave range on the basis of theoretical insights and the unique equipment of the Institute of Applied Physics. They were used for producing image visualization systems with regard to weapon detection in a human body as well as for producing a submillimeter microscope.

At the same period pioneering investigations were carried out as concerns the effects of anomalous back scattering of dielectric particles and aerospace monitoring of the environment (1970s – 1980s).<ref name="Space">{{cite book |last= L. К. Zyatkov, B.S. Elepov.  |date= 2007|title= At the origins of satellite-based aircraft monitoring of natural environment ("Space" – doc. program 'Sibir"): monograph |language= ru|location= Novosibirsk |publisher= SGGA }}</ref>

For more than 30 years (up to 1996) Minin was a scientific advisor, general director and chief designer of the Institute of Applied Physics.<ref name="Chestnoye slovo">{{cite journal |date=14 September 2006 |title= Chestnoye slovo |language= ru|volume=37-2(503-2) }}</ref><ref name="Nasha gazeta">{{cite journal |date=28 April 2002 |title= Prokopenko N.I. Fighting science|language= ru|journal= Nasha Gazeta |volume=4 |issue=25 }}</ref><ref name="Bolshaya Medveditsa">{{cite journal |date=2002 |title= For the 70th anniversary of Vladilen Fyodorovich Minin |language= ru|journal= Journal "Bolshaya Medveditsa" |volume=1 }}</ref>
 
Over 70 types of armaments families were created under the guidance of Minin, in particular, those for the navy (passive decoy projectiles, optoelectronic systems for PK-2 (Russian:{{ill|ПК-2|ru}}), PK-10 (Russian:{{ill|ПК-10|ru}}), PK-16 (Russian:{{ill|ПК-16|ru}}) complexes and others), air force and army of the USSR and Russian Federation (aircraft launch rockets [[S-8 (rocket)|S-8]], [[S-13 rocket|S-13]] family and others). Some of them have no analogues in the world up to now and are used as a basis for further modifications.<ref name=" Discoveries made by academician Minin ">{{cite journal |date= 2002|title= Alexander Petrov. Names. Discoveries made by academician Minin. |language= ru|journal= Krasnaya Zvezda |issue=189 }}</ref><ref name="Morskoy sbornik">{{cite journal |date=2012 |title= Morskoy sbornik |language= ru|volume=1982 |issue=5 |pages=23–24 }}</ref>

Minin was also at the head of the research works for developing the techniques and algorithms for numerical simulation of physical and mechanical processes. The research conducted for the development of hardware and software formed the basis for automated computing complexes.<ref name=" Calculation Experiment Technology ">{{cite book |date=2011 |title= Vladilen F. Minin, Igor V. Minin, Oleg V. Minin. Calculation Experiment Technology. In Computation Fluid Dynamics Technologies and Applications / Ed. by Igor V. Minin and Oleg V. Minin |location= Croatia |publisher= Published by In Tech }}</ref><ref name=" Nauka v Sibiri ">{{cite journal |date=1988 |title= Nauka v Sibiri |trans-title= Newspaper |language= ru|volume=11-12 |issue=2147–2148 }}</ref><ref name=" On Calculation Experiment ">{{cite journal |date=11 September 1986  |title= Minin V.F. On Calculation Experiment, and others… |language= ru|journal= Nauka V Sibiri |volume=35 |issue=1266 }}</ref>

Minin was elected a member of the presidium of the regional branch of Siberia and the Far East of the Scientific Council of the Academy of Sciences of the Soviet Union as regards a complex problem of “Mathematical simulation” and a member of Novosibirsk territorial coordination Council for science, vocational education and policy in science and technology.<ref>Resolution of Novosibirsk region administration of 22 June 1994 . № 286</ref>

In the field of numerical techniques and algorithmization he was in charge of the research on creating efficient machine-dependent techniques and algorithms for numerical simulation of the mechanics of continua processes.

Being in charge of the investigations Minin took part in the works on adaptation of the developed algorithms and creation of the brand new parallel ones for numerical simulation, implemented on the basis of upgraded 128-processor machine PS-2000 as all-in-one decision field. Together with the display stations “Gamma” type it is incorporated in general simulation complex. This system which had no analogues in the USSR made it possible to simulate various significant nonstationary processes of the mechanics of continua.<ref name=" Microprocessor-based software and systems ">{{cite journal |date= 1989|title= Buchnev А. А., Minin V.F., Sizykh V. G. Colour halftone professional station "Gamma-7.1"  |language= ru|journal= Microprocessor-based Software and Systems |issue=5 }}</ref> By 1990-91 all the TV centres of the USSR were equipped with video-computer graphic stations GAMMA-T.

By means of the developed software-hardware complex the problems of meteoroid protection for spaceship [[Vega program|“Vega” (in “Vega-Galley” project)]] were solved.<ref name=" Vega meteoroid protection ">{{cite journal |date=1984 |title= Agureykin V.A., Anisimov S.I., Bushman A.V.. Kanel G.I., Karyagin V.P., Konstantinov A.B., Kryukov B.P., Minin V.F., Razorenov S.V., Sagdeyev R.Z., Sugak S.G., Fortov V.E. Thermophysical and gas-dynamic problems of spacecraft "Vega meteoroid protection" |language= ru|journal= ТВТ |volume=22 |pages=5 }}</ref> Pioneering works on cosmogenic safety and Earth protection against asteroids were conducted.

In physics of high-speed processes Minin solved the problem of rotating cumulative charges.<ref>Minin V.F.,  Minin I.V,  Minin O.V., Technique and equipment for cumulative jet formation without the effect of cumulative charges rotation. Patent R.F. № 2491497, published on 27.08.2013 Bul. № 24 (in Russian).</ref> He also presented and gave proof of hypercumulative charges.<ref name=" Physics of hypercumulation ">{{cite book |last=Minin V.F., Minin I.V., Minin O.V. |date=2013 |title= Physics of hypercumulation and combined cumulative charges |language= ru|location= Novosibirsk |publisher= Novopoligraphcentre }}</ref>

In the field of cumulative charges in 1969 V.F. Minin received the first empirical results with cylindrical liners. The experiments were conducted at the focal distance equal to the double value of the charge diameter for different masses of explosive charges. Soon afterwards the author's certificate for invention No. 64442 with priority was obtained of 18 June 1970.<ref name=" Physics of cumulative processes ">{{cite book |last= Trishin Yu.A.|date=2005 |title= Physics of cumulative processes |language= ru|location= Novosibirsk |publisher= Institute of Hydrodynamics named after M.A. Lavrentyev, The Siberian Division of the Russian Academy of Sciences }}</ref>

The obtained knowledge was applied for making cumulative tandem tank projectile for [[2A46 125 mm gun|2A46]]. It passed complete cycle of governmental and manufacturer's tests with positive results.<ref name=" Encyclopedia ">{{cite book |date= 2006|title= "Weapons and technologies of Russia. XXI century". Ammunition and means of destruction/ edited by Russian Minister of Defense S. Ivanov.  |trans-title= Encyclopedia |language= ru|location= Moscow|publisher= “Oruzhiye I tekhnologii” Publ }}</ref><ref name=" Catalogue ">{{cite book |date=2001 |title= А. V. Karpenko. Part 1 // Catalogue of modern Russian armaments and conversion units at international exhibitions of armament and и military equipment (1992-2001).  |language= ru|location= St-Petersburg |publisher=«Bastion» }}</ref> Under Minin's guidance the works were conducted on the investigation and production of rotating hollow charge shells with a record depth of penetration.<ref>Materials of exhibition IDEX-94, Jane's Ammunition Handbook, Ninth Edition, 2000-2001, 1995-96 issue of Jane's Armour and Artillery Upgrades</ref><ref name=" Encyclopedia " />

It was Minin who discovered a new previously unknown field of [[Shaped charge|cumulation]], i.e. hypercumulation in which a number of problems have been solved or nearly solved.<ref name=" Physics of hypercumulation " /><ref>Minin V.F Minin I.V,  Minin O.V., Techniques and devices (variants) for forming high-speed cumulative jets for  borehole perforation with deep slug-free channels and large diameter: Patent R.F. № 2412338, publ. 20.02.2011.</ref>

Under him pioneering works were conducted in the field of 3D penetrators impact mechanics.<ref name=" To Optimization of Star-Shaped Penetrators ">{{cite journal |date=1982 |title= V. S. Bondarchuk, Yu. A. Vedernikov, V. G. Dulov, and V. F. Minin. To Optimization of Star-Shaped Penetrators |journal= Izv. SO AN SSSR Ser. Tekhn. Nauk |volume=13 |issue=3 }}</ref>

Vladilen Minin is also a co-author of some discoveries in the field of high-speed processes.<ref>Certificate for Invention № 010 as of  17.7.1991</ref> 
He developed new methods of magnetic pulse [[arc welding]] with high-speed impact of the parts to be fused together and short-time welding process, and applied them to production.<ref>Author's Certificate of the USSR № 393869, authors B. А. Yablochnikov, V.F. Minin, М. S. Kachan</ref><ref>Author's Certificate of the USSR № 517431, authors V. B. Bobylev, V. F. Minin, М. S. Kachan, B. А. Yablochnikov</ref><ref>Author's Certificate of the USSR № 558463, authors V. B. Bobylev, V. F. Minin, B.A. Yablochnikov</ref><ref>Author's Certificate of the USSR №1098150 authors B.V. Ageshin, Y.V. Bayromyan, V. F. Minin, B.A. Yablochnikov</ref> The welder developed for aluminum-copper nipples of refrigerator sets and the technique for electric-and-magnetic welding were patented by many countries.

Under his leadership efficient metal casting processes were developed which have no analogues in the world.<ref>Minin V.F., Pishdhevitsky B.I., Tikhonova T.S. et al. The method of  molding and coremaking: Author's Certificate of the USSR 657908. – Б.И. – № 15. – 1979</ref><ref>Markov G. А., Minin V.F. Technique for  metal mold fabrication: Author's Certificate of the USSR 582894. – 1977</ref><ref>Minin V.F., Karanik Y. А., Sirotkin Y. А. Technique for permanent permanent mold fabrication: Author's Certificate of the USSR 476078</ref>

For the first time a complex of the radar and optoelectronic close-in jammers “Smeliy” (Brave) PK-16 (Russian:{{ill|ПК-16|ru}})) was produced. A considerable contribution into passive jamming development was made by Minin.<ref name=" EW installations in the sea ">{{cite web |url=https://flot.com/science/rv3.htm |title= EW installations in the sea |last= Y. V. Novikov, А. А. Marusenko. |website= flot.com |access-date=November 15, 2019}}</ref>

In 1991 Minin was elected a president of the Urals-Siberian Branch of the Academy of Technological Sciences and a member of the Academy Council for new information technologies.

=== Publications ===
He is an author and co-author of over 600 treatises including some monographs, and more than 100 patents and discoveries.<ref name=" ↑ Vladilen Fyodorovich Minin is 80 years old!">{{cite web |url=http://dolgoprudniy.bezformata.com/listnews/vladilenu-fedorovichu-mininu-80-let/4735968/|title= ↑ Vladilen Fyodorovich Minin is 80 years old!|website= bezformata.com|access-date=November 15, 2019}}</ref><ref name=" Minin V">{{cite web |url=http://eurasian-defence.ru/?q=node/22142 |title= Minin Vladilen Fyodorovich.|publisher=Center for military-political research |website= eurasian-defence.ru|access-date=November 15, 2019}}</ref>

== Family ==
He was married to Inna Aleksandrovna Minina. He has two sons (twins), [[Oleg Minin|Oleg]] and [[Igor Minin|Igor]],<ref name=" I know the city will be! ">{{cite web |url=http://www-sbras.nsc.ru/HBC/2002/n19/f08.html=node/22142 |title= I know the city will be!|publisher=Science in siberia|website= sbras.nsc.ru|access-date=November 15, 2019}}</ref> who are both Doctors of Technical Sciences, university professors, and corresponding members of Russian Academy of Metrology and The Russian Academy of Natural History.

== Awards ==

* [[Medal "For Labour Valour"]](1967).<ref>Decree of the Supreme Soviet of the USSR of 29 April 1967</ref>
* [[Jubilee Medal "In Commemoration of the 100th Anniversary of the Birth of Vladimir Ilyich Lenin"]] (1970).
* [[Order of the Red Banner of Labour]] (1971) – for the foundation of the Institute, professional advancement, research and development work important in special fields of physics.<ref>Decree of the Supreme Soviet of the USSR of 26 April 1971</ref>
* Bronze Medal of [[Exhibition of Achievements of National Economy|VDNKH (Exhibition of Achievements of National Economy)]] of the USSR for the achievements in the development of national economy of the USSR (Certificate 67342, 1974).
* Silver medal of VDNKH (Exhibition of Achievements of National Economy) of the USSR for the achievements in the development of national economy of the USSR (Certificate 10851, 15575, - 1977, 1981).
* Gold medal of VDNKH (Exhibition of Achievements of National Economy) of the USSR for the achievements in the development of national economy of the USSR (Certificate 2756, 1985).
* [[Order of Lenin]] (1985) for the foundation of the Institute of Applied Physics and the results achieved in the field of electronic countermeasures establishment.<ref>Decree of the Supreme Soviet of the USSR of 23 February 1985</ref>
* [[Medal "Veteran of Labour"]] (1987)<ref>Resolution of the Presidium of the Supreme Soviet of the USSR, № 220 of 23 April 1987г.</ref>
* Medal “In commemoration of the 70th anniversary of [[Cheka]] – [[KGB]] (All-Russian Special Commission for Combating, Counter-revolution, Speculation and Sabotage – Committee for State Security) (1987).
* [[USSR State Prize]] (1988) for the complex of work on the production of computer aids and technologies for computing experiment in the field of [[continuum mechanics]].<ref>Resolution of  the Central Committee of the USSR and  the Council of Ministers of the USSR № 21242 of 28 October 1988</ref>
* Award pin “Honoured Inventor within the USSR”
* Medal ”100th anniversary of Novosibirsk foundation” (2003).
* Medal ”100th anniversary of V.V. Bakhirev, the Minister of machine building” for the achievements in the development of ammunition branch and long-term dedicated work (2016).
